title: Mahmud Ghaznavi Mosque
subtitle: Excavated 11th-century mosque below Raja Gira Castle, Udegram, Lower Swat

landmark.name: Mahmud Ghaznavi Mosque
edits: The mosque is drawn from the plan in the Wikipedia article: a rectangular prayer hall 28 m by 21 m, the mihrab square and centred in the west wall, an off-centre entrance in the east wall, a paved courtyard with a sunken ablution tank in the middle, three oblong rooms (ziyada) to the north and three bastions on their outer side. Front faces the qibla (254 degrees, computed from the coordinates).

Estimated, not published: the pillar base positions (5 by 8 as the article gives them), the tank size, the wall thickness and height (about 1.6 m, from the photos; the article mentions traces of 30-foot walls, which are not drawn at full height), the mihrab projection, the stone stair on the east side and the boulders.

The levelled ground is a 22 m radius terrace; the platform is 32 m by 34 m (estimated) and its straight stone retaining walls sit on the downhill sides (the article says the mosque stands on an early artificial terrace); the slope beyond it is the DEM.
The OSM archaeological-site outline (about 73 m by 33 m) is not drawn as a footprint; the walking circle is a 36 m circle around the point, not a mapped path.
Trees within 45 m of the mosque are left out so it can be seen; WorldCover 2021 maps tree cover there.
